title: Get Help page: choose a layout
question: Three layouts for the Get Help page, the page for people asking for themselves or their child. All three use the home page's look. Pick one, add a note to steer it, or re-roll for three different layouts. Volunteer and Give follow on this same page.

options.label: Promise band
options.thesis: Open on three plain promises set like the mission band, then answer the practical questions in the home page's two-column layout.
options.viewport: Title, lede and Ask for help at left; below them a centered band of three promises: free or reduced cost, open to everyone, kept private.
options.risk: The most familiar of the three; it borrows the home page's rhythm instead of giving this page a shape of its own.

options.label: The letter
options.thesis: The page is a letter to someone unsure about asking, with the practical facts beside it as margin notes.
options.viewport: A centered letter in the serif voice; margin notes for cost, privacy and what to have ready; Ask for help closes the letter.
options.risk: Prose asks for patience; someone scanning for cost has to find it in the margin.

options.label: Intake reference
options.thesis: Everything an applicant needs in one scannable reference, with a jump list and the action always in reach.
options.viewport: Title across the top; a sticky jump list at left (Who can ask, Cost, What to have ready, Privacy, Questions) with Ask for help under it; the answers run in the wide right column.
options.risk: Efficient but plain; it can feel more like a help center than a ministry.
